1

Two tabs, and one showed only half your branches

not approved

NOT APPROVED

Which control: nothing to press — it happened by itself with two tabs of the planner open on the same computer.

"I have two different tabs open on the computer. And one pulled out the branches, the other tab had half the branches."

now

One tab showed every branch; the other showed only Willingboro, Health and Family. I have not reproduced it yet, so I have nothing honest to picture as an AFTER.

after

I need one thing from you when it happens again: in BOTH tabs press Export and keep the two files. That names the difference exactly, instead of me guessing a third time.

where this stands

I was wrong twice and I am saying so. My first theory was that a partial tab writes delete records for branches it never had. I wrote the test for it: two tabs, one holding the whole planner, one holding three branches. Every branch survived on both tabs and in the cloud — so that theory is dead, and the fix I was about to build would have fixed nothing.

No AFTER picture, on purpose. A picture of a fix I cannot prove is worse than no picture. This card stays NOT APPROVED until the two Export files show me the real difference.

3

“Set up my planner” keeps coming back

approved

APPROVED

Which control: nothing to press — it is seeded at sign-in.

"Every time I log in the planner it makes a Set up my planner with the subtask with it, it's generic set up, and I don't want it. That's only for new account and mine is established account."

now

The first-run seed ran again on an account that already has a planner, so the demo task and its subtasks came back after signing in.

after

The seed now refuses to run when the account is signed in, when a cloud copy exists, or when this browser has ever held a sign-in. A genuinely new account still gets it.

where this stands

Guarded three ways, because any one of them alone can be false on a fresh browser: a signed-in user, a stored cloud copy, or any Firebase sign-in key in this browser. The seed now returns immediately if any of the three is true.

Being straight with you about the proof: I could not make the demo task come back on your build in a test — three attempts, and each time the planner loaded normally. So the AFTER picture above shows the guard is in and nothing else changed; it is not a picture of the bug being caught in the act. If it appears again after this ships, that tells us the seed is not where it comes from, and I will say so rather than quietly adding a fourth guard.

5

Complete shows everything you have completed

approved

APPROVED

Which control: Settings in the top bar → the Completed button above the tree.

"The complete button in the setting must show all the completed items. I had it on the settings section. I need to show me what each button would do until I reach to the completed tasks."

now

Pressing Completed (7) listed none of the seven finished tasks and left three unrelated branches on screen instead. Measured on your build: 7 completed, 0 shown.

after

Pressing Completed (7) lists every finished task with the branch it came from. Measured on the new build: 6 entries covering all 7 (a finished task inside a finished one is listed once, under its parent).

where this stands

every step, because you asked to see each button

Why it was empty, found by measuring not guessing: the view only ever hid and showed rows already drawn on screen. Every one of your completed tasks sits inside a folded branch, so it had no row to show — while three branches that happened to be overdue stayed visible because an !important rule beat the code trying to hide them. It now builds the list from your data, the way Deleted already did.

The same bug was in Deleted and is fixed in the same pass: 0 stray rows now, at four phone widths and on the computer.

7

Focus session: pick which priority items show

approved

APPROVED

Which control: the new Items row in the focus session panel — press the band, then Items.

"For focus session, I want to have a button option there to search priority and select the ones that should only show on the schedule."

now

A session could only be pointed at a whole branch. If a branch held forty tasks, all forty counted as belonging to that hour.

after

A new Items row opens a search box and a checklist of every priority. Tick the ones this session is for and only those count — ticking a parent brings its children with it. No ticks means the whole branch, exactly as today.

where this stands

what the button opens

Measured: ticking a parent includes everything under it; ticking a parent and its own child still counts once; two items in different branches add up correctly; a deleted item is skipped rather than breaking the session.

8

Change one session's length without changing them all

approved

APPROVED

Which control: the From or To time in the focus session panel, and the drag handles on the band.

"I want to have the ability to change a duration of a focus session without changing the whole future session. What do you think is the best way, maybe have a pop up saying save future session too?"

now

Changing the hours of a repeating session moved every future week with it, and there was no way back.

after

Changing the hours asks first: Just Fri 18 Sep or Every week. One day changes only that day; every week behaves as before. Opening the panel and changing nothing asks nothing.

where this stands

Measured, both answers: “Just Fri 18 Sep” leaves the weekly session at 09:00–11:00 and gives Friday its own hours; “Every week” moves the weekly session itself. Tuesday and Wednesday were checked and did not move.

And it undoes cleanly: delete the one changed day and that day goes straight back to the normal hours — the repeating session never stored anything about the exception, which is what keeps two devices from disagreeing about it.
